paper_title: A Persian Vision-Language-Action Dataset and Benchmark for Ambiguity- and Infeasibility-Aware Instruction-to-Plan Grounding
reason: 이 논문은 페르시아어 단일 이미지 기반 VLA 데이터셋(258개 인스턴스, 230장 사진)과 PGOS-FA 지표를 새로 제안하므로 재사용 가능한 벤치마크 후보로 볼 수 있다. 그러나 과제 언어가 페르시아어(Persian-only)여서 이 인벤토리의 한국어/영어 범위 밖이며, 영어는 시스템 프롬프트 언어 비교일 뿐 번역된 데이터가 아니라고 논문 스스로 밝힌다(III-F). 또한 PDF가 데이터셋·코드의 공식 URL을 전혀 밝히지 않고 '합리적 요청 시 제공'이라고만 적어 '링크' 증거를 채울 수 없다. 따라서 링크 근거가 없어 propose할 수 없고, 언어 범위도 맞지 않아 변경안은 제출하지 않는다.

screening.paper_title: A Persian Vision-Language-Action Dataset and Benchmark for Ambiguity- and Infeasibility-Aware Instruction-to-Plan Grounding
screening.abstract: Converting natural-language instructions into executable action plans conditioned on a scene image is a core capability for embodied human-robot interaction, but existing benchmarks target English, simulated or video-grounded environments, and largely assume instructions are clear and executable. We introduce the first Persian vision-language-action dataset for this task: 258 instances over 230 real household/office photographs, annotated with reference plans, deliberate ambiguity and infeasibility labels, disambiguating question-answer pairs, and an auto-generated chain-of-thought rationale for training. Using this resource, we ablate retrieval-augmentation, chain-of-thought prompting, and an agentic disambiguation step, evaluated with an LLM-as-judge protocol and a new metric, PGOS-FA, extending prior work (PG2S) with step-order sensitivity, an over-generation penalty, and Persian-adapted embeddings. Paired statistical testing across 36 comparisons shows retrieval-augmentation is a large, robustly significant effect, while finer-grained additions are directionally consistent but not statistically distinguishable from noise at this scale, and the LLM-judge metric has near-zero power where PGOS-FA succeeds. A blind human-correlation study on 79 real outputs shows PGOS-FA tracks human judgment at least as closely as the LLM-judge. Testing generalization beyond the ablation's single backbone, we find that most of the gap between an open-weight and a substantially stronger closed planner is attributable to open-weight model generation rather than to the closed model's capability specifically, and that our best configuration significantly outperforms an independently reproduced external baseline despite a weaker backbone. The dataset, PGOS-FA implementation, and evaluation code will be made available upon reasonable request.
